desc: Prove reversal preserves feasibility/cost: each nums subarray maps bijectively to a b subarray, and cost to make non-decreasing equals cost to make the reversed one non-increasing.
Derive the window cost formula in b: cost = sum over positions of (suffix max within window - b[pos]).

Implement reverse + two-pointer with a monotonic deque of strictly-decreasing suffix-max (value,count) groups, tracking total_sufmax and total_sum; add-right pops groups with value <= x, remove-left decrements/pops the leftmost group and relies on the fact that deleting the leftmost position leaves all other suffix maxima unchanged.

Test on examples 1 and 2 and edge cases (n=1, increasing, decreasing, all equal, k=1, huge k); confirm the O(n) deque solution passes and fix any off-by-one or comparison errors (use <= when merging on add).
